text:
Maya (PM): Drafted a short PRD for prompt-level gating + fallback routing. Want engineering and ML feedback before we lock acceptance criteria. TL;DR: route individual calls based on safety/latency/cost signals, fall back to cheaper or smaller models when needed. Link: https://tiny.redwood/prd-prompt-gating

Devin (Eng): skimmed it. biggest perf concern is per-request classification overhead and route hop penalty. do we do sync classifier inline or async cost estimation?

Elena (ML Eng): we should run a lightweight safety and complexity classifier inline (<2ms target). if classifier is too slow we negate gains. also need clear thresholds per workload (chat vs embedding).

Sam (SRE): SLOs to consider: p95 end-to-end <= 350ms for chat small contexts; error rate delta < 1% during rollout. also need throttles for model fallback to avoid capacity storms.

Jordan (Solutions): customers asked for deterministic routing for compliance customers (must opt-out of fallback to smaller models). include a per-customer policy flag in the design.

Maya (PM): good call. Acceptance criteria proposal:
- Functional: gating routes >95% of calls correctly on our held-out eval (safety/quality).
- Performance: end-to-end p95 for gated path <= 350ms (measured on hosted infra).
- Cost: reduce avg per-token cost for gated traffic by >=15% in baseline workloads.
- Reliability: no more than 1% absolute increase in overall error-rate during 5% canary.
- Observability: dashboards showing gate decisions, classifier score distribution, and per-model traffic splits.

Devin (Eng): implementation notes:
- classifier runs in-serving on CPU threads (C++) with vectorized code, model-agnostic features (prompt length, token density, safety score).
- route table config: JSON per-customer with keys: `allow_fallback`, `latency_priority`, `safety_thresholds`
- example config:
```
{
  "allow_fallback": true,
  "latency_priority": "balanced",
  "safety_thresholds": {"chat": 0.85, "embed": 0.9}
}
```

Elena (ML Eng): classifier thresholds: we need to calibrate on multi-turn chat evals and embedding queries separately. edge-case: long system prompts + short user query can flip decision; ensure we compute features on the full request (system+history+input).

Sam (SRE): rollout plan suggestion:
- stage 0: internal dogfood on non-critical tenants (0% external)
- stage 1: 5% external canary for 48h with auto-rollback if error-rate +1% or p95 latency +5%
- stage 2: 25% if stable for 7d
- stage 3: ramp to 100% with incremental policy tuning

Maya (PM): edge cases we should capture in PRD:
- rerank flows that use embeddings + cross-encoder: ensure gating doesn't split multi-call pipelines incorrectly
- caching: prefix/KV cache validity when model variant changes
- deterministic routing for compliance customers
- tokenization differences between model variants causing length regressions

Jordan (Solutions): add an acceptance test scenario: customer-simulated burst with 10k concurrent chat calls, validate fallback doesn't saturate cheaper models and we preserve graceful degradation. include runbook steps for fallback saturation.

Devin (Eng): will prototype classifier with a 1-layer logistic regressor over hashed n-grams + length, should be trivial to A/B. will push a feature branch next week.

Elena (ML Eng): I'll prepare a 300-sample eval set covering chat, embedding, and rerank pipelines to calibrate thresholds and to define quality regression guards.

Sam (SRE): I'll add SLO checks and create alert playbooks: high fallback rate, high classifier score drift, model capacity saturation. also we should log per-request routing metadata for 30 days.

Maya (PM): Nice. Open questions:
- do we support multi-hop fallbacks (e.g., medium -> small -> tiny)? tradeoffs?
- how do we surface fallback decisions to customers (headers / response metadata)?

Devin (Eng): multi-hop possible but complicates caching and billing. prefer single fallback for MVP, reserve multi-tier for Dedicated customers.

Jordan (Solutions): surface via response metadata: `x-rw-model-used` and `x-rw-fallback-reason` are sufficient. customers love observability.

deploy-bot: CI passed for `feature/prompt-gating-proto`. preview env: https://preview.redwood/prompt-gating

Maya (PM): thanks all — next steps: Devin + Elena sync Monday to pick classifier API and metrics; Sam to draft rollout playbook; Jordan to add customer acceptance test; I'll update PRD acceptance criteria and freeze for engineering scoping on Thursday. Please add comments inline on the doc by EOD Wednesday. :thumbsup:

Devin (Eng): noted, will add initial design doc link in comments.

Elena (ML Eng): pinged with eval dataset link.

Sam (SRE): creating alert rules now.

Jordan (Solutions): prepping customer sample scenarios.

Maya (PM): closing loop — thanks everyone!
